title: Exercise 1.4 · Q7(ii)
summary: If x=2+3i and x_max=1+2√3i, calculate the frequency when t=2.
alt: Exercise 1.4 · Q7(ii): If x=2+3i and x_max=1+2√3i, calculate the frequency when t=2.

z.label: The number z
z.text: The complex number you are given.

zb.label: Second number / conjugate
zb.text: The conjugate, or the second number.

steps.title: Use x=x_maxe^(iω t)
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\text{Start at $x_{\max}$ when $t=0$ and turn at}\\[5pt]&\text{a steady rate $\omega$.}\\[5pt]&e^{i\omega t}=\dfrac{x}{x_{\max}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Angle turned in 2 seconds
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\omega t=\theta=\arg x-\arg x_{\max}\approx -0.307\ \text{rad}\ (-17.6^\circ)\\[5pt]&\text{This is the angle found in part (i).}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Frequency
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&f=\dfrac{|\omega|}{2\pi}\approx\textcolor{#047857}{\mathbf{0.0244\ \text{Hz}}}\\[5pt]&\text{The minus sign in $\omega$ only means}\\[5pt]&\text{the turn is clockwise; a frequency is}\\[5pt]&\text{taken as positive.}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: If the turn must be anticlockwise
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\text{Then the particle reaches $x$ after a}\\[5pt]&\text{turn of $2\pi+\theta$ instead.}\\[5pt]&\omega=\dfrac{2\pi+\theta}{2}\approx 2.988\ \text{rad/s},\qquad f\approx 0.4756\ \text{Hz}\\[5pt]&\text{Your teacher may expect either; the}\\[5pt]&\text{first is what the formula gives}\\[5pt]&\text{directly.}\end{aligned}\]
